quandoUsar: Highlight cards in a showcase or product page, such as a travel destination or a boarding pass, where depth draws attention to a few items.
When parts of the content should float above the face: each `TiltCardLayer` rises `depth` px during hover and shifts against the background as the card tilts.
quandoEvitar: Use `card` for ordinary cards in lists and panels, where the motion would only distract.
Use `wallet-card` for a payment card that also flips to show the back.
In interfaces used mostly by touch the effect is lost: the card only tilts with a mouse.
acessibilidade: It is a visual container, with no role or focus of its own: if the whole card leads somewhere, put a link or button with the action text inside it.
The tilt only responds to the mouse; keyboard, touch, pen, and screen readers don't perceive it, so no information should depend on it.
The glare is `aria-hidden` and has `pointer-events: none`, so links and buttons beneath it stay clickable.
movimento: The card rotates up to `maxTilt` degrees (10 by default) at the edges, following the cursor with a firm spring and no bounce, scales up to `hoverScale`, and shows a glare at the cursor position.
On leaving, it returns to flat on a spring; the `TiltCardLayer` layers rise with the hover and return to the face at rest, where the text is sharp.
With “reduced motion” on, as with `disabled`, the card stays flat: no rotation, no scale, no glare, and no raised layers.
desempenho: The card keeps `will-change: transform` all the time (except with “reduced motion”), which reserves a compositing layer per instance; in a grid with dozens of them, use the effect only on highlights.
notasIA: Import `TiltCard` (and `TiltCardLayer`, if you want layers) from `@/components/ryan-ui/tilt-card/tilt-card`; set width and height via `className` or `style`, because the inner card fills the container's height.
Every element between the card and the layers needs `transform-style: preserve-3d`, like the boarding pass body in the demo; without it the layers flatten onto the face.
The card doesn't clip its content: for a cover image, use `position: absolute`, `inset: 0`, and `border-radius: inherit`; `onTiltChange` fires on every mouse movement, so avoid heavy state there.
